title: Chapter 2 — Primates
description: The order that includes humans and their closest relatives. Divided into Strepsirrhini (wet-nosed primates: lemurs, lorises) and Haplorhini (dry-nosed: tarsiers, monkeys, apes). Primates are characterised by forward-facing eyes, grasping hands, and relatively large brains. Around 500 living species.

children.name: Gorilla
children.description: The largest living primates, native to the forests of central Africa. Gorillas are highly social, living in groups led by a dominant silverback male, and are primarily terrestrial herbivores. Critically endangered due to habitat loss, poaching, and disease.

children.name: Gorilla gorilla
children.description: The western gorilla (Gorilla gorilla) is a great ape found in Africa, one of two species of the hominine genus Gorilla.

children.name: Gorilla beringei
children.description: The eastern gorilla (Gorilla beringei) is a critically endangered species of the genus Gorilla and the largest living primate.

children.name: Pan
children.description: Humans' closest living relatives, sharing approximately 98.7% of DNA with Homo sapiens. Pan comprises two species — the common chimpanzee and the bonobo — both confined to the forests of central Africa and distinguished by markedly different social structures.

children.name: Pan troglodytes
children.description: The chimpanzee (; Pan troglodytes), also simply known as the chimp, is an endangered species of great ape native to the forests and savannahs of tropical Africa.

children.name: Pan paniscus
children.description: The bonobo (; Pan paniscus), also historically called the pygmy chimpanzee (less often the dwarf chimpanzee or gracile chimpanzee), is an endangered great ape and one of the two species making up the genus Pan (the other being the common chimpanzee, Pan troglodytes).

children.name: Pongo
children.description: The only great apes native to Asia, orangutans inhabit the tropical rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra. They are the most arboreal of the great apes and the most solitary, with a highly developed intelligence and exceptionally long inter-birth intervals.

children.name: Pongo pygmaeus
children.description: The Bornean orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus) is an orangutan species endemic to the island of Borneo.

children.name: Pongo abelii
children.description: The Sumatran orangutan (Pongo abelii) is one of the three species of orangutans.

children.name: Pongo tapanuliensis
children.description: The Tapanuli orangutan (Pongo tapanuliensis) is a species of orangutan restricted to South Tapanuli in the island of Sumatra in Indonesia.

children.name: Homo
children.description: A genus of bipedal great apes with exceptionally large brains, arising in Africa roughly 2–3 million years ago. At least a dozen species are known from the fossil record, though only Homo sapiens survives today. Several archaic species — including Neanderthals and Denisovans — interbred with modern humans, leaving traces in living genomes.

children.name: Homo sapiens
children.description: Humans (Homo sapiens, meaning 'thinking man' or 'wise man') are the most abundant and widespread species of primates, characterized by bipedalism, minimal body hair, and large, complex brains enabling the development of advanced technology, culture, and language..

children.name: Homo neanderthalensis
children.description: Neanderthals ( nee-AN-də(r)-TAHL, nay-, -⁠THAHL; Homo neanderthalensis or sometimes Homo sapiens neanderthalensis) are an extinct group of archaic humans who inhabited Europe and Western and Central Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene..

children.name: Homo denisova
children.description: The Denisovans or Denisova hominins ( də-NIS-ə-və(nz)) are an extinct species or subspecies of archaic human that ranged across Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene, approximately 200,000–32,000 years ago..

children.name: Homo heidelbergensis
children.description: Homo heidelbergensis () is a species of archaic human from the Middle Pleistocene of Europe and Africa, as well as potentially Asia depending on the taxonomic convention used.

children.name: Homo erectus
children.description: Homo erectus is an extinct species of archaic human from the Pleistocene, spanning nearly 2 million years. It is the first human species to evolve a humanlike body plan and gait, to leave Africa and colonize Asia and Europe, and to wield fire. Some populations of H.

children.name: Homo habilis
children.description: Homo habilis ( 'handy man') is an extinct species of archaic human from the Early Pleistocene of East and South Africa about 2.4 million years ago to 1.65 million years ago (mya).

children.name: Homo floresiensis
children.description: Homo floresiensis, also known as "Flores Man" or "Hobbit", is an extinct species of small archaic humans that inhabited the island of Flores, Indonesia, until the arrival of modern humans about 50,000 years ago.

children.name: Homo naledi
children.description: Homo naledi is an extinct species of archaic human discovered in 2013 in the Rising Star Cave system, Gauteng province, South Africa, part of the Cradle of Humankind, dating back to the Middle Pleistocene 335,000–236,000 years ago.

children.name: Australopithecus
children.description: Extinct bipedal hominins from Africa, living roughly 2–4 million years ago. Australopithecus walked upright but retained many ape-like features including small brains and long arms. The famous fossil 'Lucy' (A. afarensis) is among the best-known human ancestors, demonstrating that upright walking preceded the evolution of large brains.

children.name: Australopithecus afarensis
children.description: Australopithecus afarensis is an extinct species of australopithecine which lived from about 3.9–2.9 million years ago (mya) in the Pliocene of East Africa. The first fossils were discovered in the 1930s, but major fossil finds would not take place until the 1970s. From 1972 to 1977, the International Afar Research Expedition—led by anthropologists Maurice Taieb, Donald Johanson and Yves Coppens—unearthed several hundreds of hominin specimens in Hadar, Afar Region, Ethiopia, the most significant being the exceedingly well-preserved skeleton AL 288-1 ("Lucy") and the site AL 333.

children.name: Australopithecus africanus
children.description: Australopithecus africanus is an extinct species of australopithecine which lived between about 3.3 and 2.1 million years ago in the Late Pliocene to Early Pleistocene of South Africa.

children.name: Australopithecus sediba
children.description: Australopithecus sediba is an extinct species of australopithecine recovered from Malapa Cave, Cradle of Humankind, South Africa.

children.name: Australopithecus anamensis
children.description: Australopithecus anamensis is a hominin species that lived roughly between 4.3 and 3.8 million years ago, and is the oldest known Australopithecus species.

children.name: Paranthropus
children.description: The robust australopithecines — a side-branch of the human family tree with massively developed jaw muscles and large, flat molars adapted for grinding tough plant material. Despite their formidable chewing apparatus, they were not direct human ancestors but a parallel evolutionary experiment that eventually died out.

children.name: Paranthropus boisei
children.description: Paranthropus boisei is a species of australopithecine from the Early Pleistocene of East Africa about 2.5 to 1.15 million years ago.

children.name: Paranthropus robustus
children.description: Paranthropus robustus is a species of robust australopithecine from the Early and possibly Middle Pleistocene of the Cradle of Humankind, South Africa, about 2.27 to 0.87 (or, more conservatively, 2 to 1) million years ago.

children.name: Macaca
children.description: The most geographically widespread primate genus after Homo, with over 20 species distributed from Gibraltar to Japan. Macaques are highly adaptable, thriving in tropical forests, snowy mountains, and urban environments alike, and are widely used in biomedical research.

children.name: Macaca mulatta
children.description: The rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), colloquially rhesus monkey, is a species of Old World monkey in the Macaca genus.

children.name: Macaca fascicularis
children.description: Macaca fascicularis, variously known by common names such as crab-eating macaque, long-tailed macaque, or cynomolgus monkey, is a macaque species native to Southeast Asia..

children.name: Macaca fuscata
children.description: The Japanese macaque (Macaca fuscata), also known as the snow monkey, is a terrestrial Old World monkey species that is native to Japan.

children.name: Macaca sylvanus
children.description: The Barbary macaque (Macaca sylvanus) is a macaque species native to the Atlas Mountains of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia, along with a small introduced population in Gibraltar.

children.name: Macaca nigra
children.description: The Celebes crested macaque (Macaca nigra), also known as the crested black macaque, Sulawesi crested macaque, or the black ape, is an Old World monkey that lives in the tropical regions of north Sulawesi.

children.name: Macaca nemestrina
children.description: The southern pig-tailed macaque (Macaca nemestrina), also known as the Sundaland pig-tailed macaque and the Sunda pig-tailed macaque, is a medium-sized macaque that lives in Sundaland, southern Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia..

children.name: Macaca thibetana
children.description: The Tibetan macaque (Macaca thibetana), also known as Père David's Macaque, This species lives in subtropical forests (mixed deciduous to evergreen) at elevations from above sea level.

children.name: Macaca arctoides
children.description: The stump-tailed macaque (Macaca arctoides), also called the bear macaque, is a species of macaque native to South Asia and Southeast Asia..

children.name: Macaca radiata
children.description: The bonnet macaque (Macaca radiata), also known as zati, is a species of macaque endemic to southern India.

children.name: Macaca silenus
children.description: The lion-tailed macaque, locally called wanderoo, is an Old World monkey endemic to the Western Ghats of South India.

children.name: Macaca tonkeana
children.description: The Tonkean black macaque or Tonkean macaque (Macaca tonkeana) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Macaca maura
children.description: The Moor macaque (Macaca maura) is a macaque species with brown/black body fur with a pale rump patch and pink bare skin on the rump.

children.name: Macaca ochreata
children.description: The booted macaque (Macaca ochreata) is a macaque of the Sulawesi Island, Indonesia.

children.name: Macaca nigrescens
children.description: The Gorontalo macaque or Dumoga-bone macaque (Macaca nigrescens) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Macaca hecki
children.description: The Heck's macaque (Macaca hecki) is a macaque of Sulawesi, Indonesia..

children.name: Macaca leonina
children.description: The northern pig-tailed macaque (Macaca leonina) is a vulnerable species of macaque in the subfamily Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Macaca pagensis
children.description: The Pagai Island macaque (Macaca pagensis), also known as the Pagai macaque or Bokkoi, is an Old World monkey endemic to the Mentawai Islands off the west coast of Sumatra..

children.name: Macaca siberu
children.description: The Siberut macaque is a vulnerable species of macaque, which is endemic to Siberut Island in Indonesia. It was formerly considered conspecific with the Pagai Island macaque which is overall paler in color, but this arrangement was polyphyletic. Both were formerly considered subspecies of the southern pig-tailed macaque.

children.name: Macaca cyclopis
children.description: The Formosan rock macaque (Macaca cyclopis), also known as the Formosan rock monkey or Taiwanese macaque, is a macaque endemic to the island of Taiwan, which has also been introduced to Japan..

children.name: Macaca munzala
children.description: The Arunachal macaque is a macaque native to Eastern Himalayas of Bhutan, China and India. It is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.

children.name: Macaca brunnescens
children.description: Found on Buton Island and several small adjacent islands off southeastern Sulawesi, sometimes treated as a subspecies of M. ochreata. Its restricted range and ongoing habitat loss place it in the Vulnerable category on the IUCN Red List.

children.name: Papio
children.description: Baboons are large, terrestrial Old World monkeys native to the open woodlands and savannas of Africa and Arabia. They live in multi-male, multi-female troops of up to 200 individuals and are among the most successful primates on the continent.

children.name: Papio anubis
children.description: The olive baboon (Papio anubis), also called the Anubis baboon, is a member of the family Cercopithecidae Old World monkeys.

children.name: Papio cynocephalus
children.description: The yellow baboon (Papio cynocephalus) is a baboon in the family of Old World monkeys.

children.name: Papio ursinus
children.description: The chacma baboon (Papio ursinus), also known as the Cape baboon, is, like all other baboons, from the Old World monkey family.

children.name: Papio hamadryas
children.description: The hamadryas baboon (Papio hamadryas ; ; ) is a species of baboon within the Old World monkey family.

children.name: Papio kindae
children.description: The Kinda baboon (Papio kindae) is a species of baboon present in the miombo woodlands of Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia, and possibly western Tanzania.

children.name: Papio papio
children.description: The Guinea baboon (Papio papio) is a baboon from the Old World monkey family.

children.name: Mandrillus
children.description: The mandrill is the world's largest monkey and the most colourful mammal, with males displaying vivid blue and red facial markings that intensify with dominance. Both species inhabit the rainforests of west-central Africa and live in large multi-male groups.

children.name: Mandrillus sphinx
children.description: The mandrill (Mandrillus sphinx) is a large Old World monkey native to west central Africa..

children.name: Mandrillus leucophaeus
children.description: The drill (Mandrillus leucophaeus) is a primate of the family Cercopithecidae (Old World monkeys), related to baboons and even more closely to the mandrill..

children.name: Theropithecus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the gelada, a grass-eating monkey of the Ethiopian highlands and the only surviving member of a once-diverse lineage. Geladas live in the largest primate groups of any non-human, with herds of up to 600 individuals.

children.name: Theropithecus gelada
children.description: The gelada (Theropithecus gelada, Amharic: ጭላዳ, romanized: č̣əlada, Oromo: Jaldeessa daabee), sometimes called the bleeding-heart monkey or the gelada baboon, is a species of Old World monkey found only in the Ethiopian Highlands, living at elevations of 1,800–4,400 m (5,900–14,400 ft) above sea level..

children.name: Cercocebus
children.description: Mangabeys are medium-sized, semi-terrestrial monkeys of African lowland forests, closely related to mandrills and baboons. They are specialist hard-object feeders, with robust jaws and deep molar reliefs allowing them to crack seeds and pods that other monkeys cannot exploit.

children.name: Cercocebus torquatus
children.description: The collared mangabey (Cercocebus torquatus), also called red-capped mangabey and white-collared mangabey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae of Old World monkeys.

children.name: Cercocebus atys
children.description: The sooty mangabey (Cercocebus atys) is an Old World monkey found in forests from Senegal in a margin along the coast down to the Ivory Coast.

children.name: Cercocebus agilis
children.description: The agile mangabey (Cercocebus agilis) is an Old World monkey of the white-eyelid mangabey group found in swampy forests of Central Africa in Equatorial Guinea, Cameroon, Gabon, Central African Republic, Republic of Congo, and DR Congo.

children.name: Cercocebus chrysogaster
children.description: The golden-bellied mangabey (Cercocebus chrysogaster) is an Endangered Old World monkey found in swampy, humid forests south of the Congo River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo..

children.name: Cercocebus galeritus
children.description: The Tana River mangabey (Cercocebus galeritus) is a highly endangered species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercocebus lunulatus
children.description: The white-naped mangabey (Cercocebus lunulatus) is a species of Old World monkey in the subfamily Cercopithecinae..

children.name: Lophocebus
children.description: Black mangabeys are arboreal Old World monkeys of central African forests, more closely related to baboons than to the semi-terrestrial Cercocebus mangabeys despite their similar appearance — a classic example of convergent evolution. They bear conspicuous crests and eyelid colouration.

children.name: Lophocebus albigena
children.description: The grey-cheeked mangabey (Lophocebus albigena), also known as the white-cheeked mangabey, is an Old World monkey found in the forests of Central Africa..

children.name: Lophocebus aterrimus
children.description: The black crested mangabey (Lophocebus aterrimus) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Lophocebus johnstoni
children.description: Johnston's mangabey (Lophocebus albigena johnstoni) is a subspecies of the gray-cheeked mangabey (L..

children.name: Lophocebus opdenboschi
children.description: Opdenbosch's mangabey (Lophocebus aterrimus opdenboschi) is a subspecies of crested mangabey in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Rungwecebus
children.description: A monotypic genus erected in 2005 for the kipunji, the first new African monkey genus described in 83 years. Discovered independently by two field teams in Tanzania's Southern Highlands and Udzungwa Mountains, the kipunji was initially misidentified as a Lophocebus mangabey.

children.name: Rungwecebus kipunji
children.description: The kipunji (Rungwecebus kipunji), also known as the highland mangabey, is a species of Old World monkey that lives in the highland forests of Tanzania..

children.name: Cercopithecus
children.description: The guenons — a large, diverse genus of small to medium-sized forest monkeys — are the most species-rich primate genus in Africa. Each species typically has a distinctive facial pattern, which facilitates species recognition in the mixed-species groups they often form.

children.name: Cercopithecus mitis
children.description: The blue monkey or diademed monkey (Cercopithecus mitis) is a species of Old World monkey native to Central and East Africa, ranging from the upper Congo River basin east to the East African Rift and south to northern Angola and Zambia and populations further south down to South Africa.

children.name: Cercopithecus diana
children.description: The Diana monkey (Cercopithecus diana) is an Old World monkey found in the high canopy forests in Sierra Leone, Liberia, and western Côte d'Ivoire Named for its white brow which is said to resemble the bow of the Roman goddess Diana, this black-grey guenon has a white throat, crescent-shaped browband, ruff and beard.

children.name: Cercopithecus neglectus
children.description: De Brazza's monkey (Cercopithecus neglectus) is an Old World monkey endemic to the riverine and swamp forests of central Africa..

children.name: Cercopithecus nictitans
children.description: The greater spot-nosed monkey or putty-nosed monkey (Cercopithecus nictitans) is one of the smallest Old World monkeys..

children.name: Cercopithecus petaurista
children.description: The lesser spot-nosed monkey (Cercopithecus petaurista), also known as the lesser spot-nosed guenon, lesser white-nosed guenon, or lesser white-nosed monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus ascanius
children.description: The red-tailed monkey (Cercopithecus ascanius), also known as the black-cheeked white-nosed monkey, red-tailed guenon, redtail monkey, or Schmidt's guenon, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus cephus
children.description: thumb|3d model of the skeleton The moustached guenon or moustached monkey (Cercopithecus cephus) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Cercopithecus mona
children.description: The mona monkey (Cercopithecus mona) is an Old World monkey that lives in western Africa between Ghana and Cameroon.

children.name: Cercopithecus campbelli
children.description: Campbell's mona monkey (Cercopithecus campbelli), also known as Campbell's guenon and Campbell's monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae found in the Ivory Coast, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Senegal, and Sierra Leone..

children.name: Cercopithecus lowei
children.description: Lowe's mona monkey (Cercopithecus lowei) is an Old World monkey in the family Cercopithecidae found from the Ivory Coast to Ghana..

children.name: Cercopithecus pogonias
children.description: The crested mona monkey, also known as the crowned guenon, crowned monkey, golden-bellied guenon, or golden-bellied monkey, (Cercopithecus pogonias), is a species of African primate in the family Cercopithecidae found in west central Africa..

children.name: Cercopithecus erythrogaster
children.description: The white-throated guenon (Cercopithecus erythrogaster), also known as the red-bellied monkey and the red-bellied guenon, is a diurnal primate that lives on trees of rainforests or tropical areas of Nigeria and Benin..

children.name: Cercopithecus erythrotis
children.description: The red-eared guenon (Cercopithecus erythrotis), also called red-eared monkey or russet-eared guenon, is a primate species in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus hamlyni
children.description: The Hamlyn's monkey (Cercopithecus hamlyni), also known as the owl-faced monkey, is a species of Old World monkey that inhabits the bamboo and primary rainforests of the Congo..

children.name: Cercopithecus wolfi
children.description: Wolf's mona monkey (Cercopithecus wolfi), also called Wolf's guenon, is a colourful Old World monkey in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Cercopithecus denti
children.description: Dent's mona monkey (Cercopithecus denti) is an Old World monkey in the family Cercopithecidae found in Central Africa..

children.name: Cercopithecus dryas
children.description: The Dryas monkey (Chlorocebus dryas), also known as Salonga monkey, ekele, or inoko, is a little-known species of Old World monkey found only in the Congo Basin, restricted to the left bank of the Congo River.

children.name: Cercopithecus roloway
children.description: The Roloway monkey (Cercopithecus roloway) is an endangered species of Old World monkey endemic to tropical West Africa.

children.name: Cercopithecus preussi
children.description: The Preuss's monkey (Allochrocebus preussi), also known as Preuss's guenon, is a diurnal primate that lives terrestrially in mountainous (up to 2500 m) forests of eastern Nigeria, western Cameroon and Bioko in Equatorial Guinea..

children.name: Cercopithecus doggetti
children.description: The silver monkey (Cercopithecus mitis doggetti) is a subspecies of the blue monkey (Cercopithecus mitis).

children.name: Cercopithecus kandti
children.description: The golden monkey (Cercopithecus mitis kandti) is a subspecies of the blue monkey.

children.name: Cercopithecus sclateri
children.description: Sclater's guenon (Cercopithecus sclateri), also known as Sclater's monkey and the Nigerian monkey, is an Old World monkey that was first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1904 and named after Philip Sclater..

children.name: Allochrocebus
children.description: A small genus of ground-dwelling guenons of central and west-central Africa, separated from Cercopithecus based on molecular and morphological evidence. These species are more terrestrial than typical guenons and inhabit montane and submontane forests.

children.name: Allochrocebus lhoesti
children.description: L'Hoest's monkey (Allochrocebus lhoesti), also known as the mountain monkey, is a guenon found in the upper eastern Congo Basin..

children.name: Allochrocebus solatus
children.description: The sun-tailed monkey (Allochrocebus solatus) from Gabon is one of the least studied primates in its habitat..

children.name: Allochrocebus preussi
children.description: The Preuss's monkey (Allochrocebus preussi), also known as Preuss's guenon, is a diurnal primate that lives terrestrially in mountainous (up to 2500 m) forests of eastern Nigeria, western Cameroon and Bioko in Equatorial Guinea..

children.name: Erythrocebus
children.description: The patas monkey is the fastest-running primate, capable of reaching 55 km/h. A specialised open-country species of the African savanna belt, it is the most terrestrial of the guenon-like monkeys and has long limbs adapted for ground locomotion.

children.name: Erythrocebus patas
children.description: The common patas monkey (Erythrocebus patas), also known as the hussar monkey, is a ground-dwelling monkey distributed over semi-arid areas of West Africa, and into East Africa.

children.name: Miopithecus
children.description: The talapoins are the smallest Old World monkeys, with a round head, large eyes, and a bright green coat. They are highly social and semi-aquatic, living in large groups along rivers and flooded forests of equatorial Africa.

children.name: Miopithecus talapoin
children.description: The Angolan talapoin (Miopithecus talapoin), also known as the southern talapoin, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Miopithecus ogouensis
children.description: The Gabon talapoin (Miopithecus ogouensis), also known as the northern talapoin, is a small species of African monkey native to riparian habitats in Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, the western Republic of the Congo and the far western Democratic Republic of Congo.

children.name: Allenopithecus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Allen's swamp monkey, the most plesiomorphic cercopithecine and a morphological outlier among the guenon lineage. It is placed in its own subfamily by some authorities due to its distinctive anatomy and behaviour.

children.name: Allenopithecus nigroviridis
children.description: Allen's swamp monkey (Allenopithecus nigroviridis) is a species of Old World monkey endemic to swamps and riparian forests in the central Congo Basin..

children.name: Chlorocebus
children.description: Vervet monkeys are among the most studied primates in the wild, renowned for their distinct alarm calls that discriminate between aerial and terrestrial predators. Highly adaptable, they occupy habitats from forest edge to semi-arid savanna across sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Chlorocebus pygerythrus
children.description: The vervet monkey (Chlorocebus pygerythrus), or simply vervet, is an Old World monkey of the family Cercopithecidae native to Africa.

children.name: Chlorocebus sabaeus
children.description: The green monkey (Chlorocebus sabaeus), also known as the sabaeus monkey, is an Old World monkey with golden-green fur and pale hands and feet.

children.name: Chlorocebus aethiops
children.description: The grivet (Chlorocebus aethiops) is an Old World monkey with long white tufts of hair along the sides of its face..

children.name: Chlorocebus tantalus
children.description: The tantalus monkey (Chlorocebus tantalus) is an Old World monkey from Africa that ranges from Ghana to Sudan.

children.name: Chlorocebus cynosuros
children.description: The malbrouck (Chlorocebus cynosuros) is an Old World primate from Africa that belongs to the genus Chlorocebus..

children.name: Chlorocebus djamdjamensis
children.description: The Bale Mountains vervet (Chlorocebus djamdjamensis) is a terrestrial Old World monkey endemic to Ethiopia, found in the bamboo forests of the Bale Mountains..

children.name: Colobus
children.description: Colobus monkeys are the only Old World monkeys that lack a thumb, an adaptation for rapid arboreal movement through forest canopies. They are specialist leaf-eaters with complex, multi-chambered stomachs that ferment tough foliage.

children.name: Colobus guereza
children.description: The mantled guereza (Colobus guereza), also known simply as the guereza, the eastern black-and-white colobus, or the Abyssinian black-and-white colobus, is a black-and-white colobus, a type of Old World monkey.

children.name: Colobus polykomos
children.description: The king colobus (Colobus polykomos), also known as the western black-and-white colobus, is a species of Old World monkey, found in lowland and mountain rainforests in a region stretching from Senegal, through Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, Sierra Leone and Liberia to the Ivory Coast.

children.name: Colobus angolensis
children.description: The Angola colobus (Colobus angolensis), Angolan black-and-white colobus, or Angolan colobus is a primate species of Old World monkey belonging to the genus Colobus.

children.name: Colobus satanas
children.description: The black colobus (Colobus satanas), or satanic black colobus, is a species of Old World monkey belonging to the genus Colobus.

children.name: Colobus vellerosus
children.description: The ursine colobus (Colobus vellerosus), also known as the white-thighed colobus, Geoffroy's black-and-white colobus, or the white-thighed black-and-white colobus, is a West African species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Piliocolobus
children.description: Red colobus monkeys, among the most hunted primates in Africa and a preferred prey of chimpanzees. Several species are critically endangered due to habitat loss and hunting pressure.

children.name: Piliocolobus badius
children.description: The western red colobus (Piliocolobus badius), also known as the bay red colobus, rust red colobus or Upper Guinea red colobus, is a species of Old World monkey in West African forests from Senegal to Ghana..

children.name: Piliocolobus tephrosceles
children.description: The Ugandan red colobus (Piliocolobus tephrosceles) or ashy red colobus is an endangered species of red colobus monkey, recognised as a distinct species since 2001..

children.name: Piliocolobus rufomitratus
children.description: The Tana River red colobus (Piliocolobus rufomitratus), also called the eastern red colobus, is a highly endangered species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Piliocolobus kirkii
children.description: The Zanzibar red colobus (Piliocolobus kirkii) is a species of red colobus monkey endemic to Unguja, the main island of the Zanzibar Archipelago, off the coast of Tanzania.

children.name: Piliocolobus gordonorum
children.description: The Udzungwa red colobus (Piliocolobus gordonorum), also known as the Uzungwa red colobus or Iringa red colobus, is a species of the primate family Cercopithecidae that is endemic to riverine and montane forests in the Udzungwa Mountains in Tanzania..

children.name: Piliocolobus foai
children.description: Foa's red colobus (Piliocolobus foai) or the Central African red colobus, is a species of red colobus monkey found in the Democratic Republic of the Congo..

children.name: Piliocolobus pennantii
children.description: Pennant's colobus or Pennant's red colobus (Piliocolobus pennantii) is a species of tree-dwelling primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Piliocolobus oustaleti
children.description: Oustalet's red colobus (Piliocolobus oustaleti) is a species of red colobus monkey..

children.name: Piliocolobus preussi
children.description: Preuss's red colobus (Piliocolobus preussi) is a red colobus primate species endemic to the Cross-Sanaga Rivers ecoregion..

children.name: Piliocolobus langi
children.description: Lang's red colobus (Piliocolobus langi) is a species of red colobus monkey..

children.name: Procolobus
children.description: A monotypic genus for the olive colobus, the smallest colobine monkey and one of the most cryptic primates of the West African rainforest. The olive colobus is the only colobine to carry its young in its mouth rather than clinging to the ventrum.

children.name: Procolobus verus
children.description: The olive colobus monkey (Procolobus verus), also known as the green colobus or Van Beneden's colobus, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae.

children.name: Semnopithecus
children.description: The grey langurs or Hanuman langurs are among the most widespread leaf monkeys of South Asia, venerated in Hinduism as representatives of the god Hanuman. They are highly tolerant of human presence and can be found in cities, temples, and farmland as well as forests.

children.name: Semnopithecus entellus
children.description: The northern plains gray langur (Semnopithecus entellus), also known as the sacred langur, Bengal sacred langur and Hanuman langur, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Semnopithecus schistaceus
children.description: The Nepal gray langur (Semnopithecus schistaceus) is a gray langur endemic to the Himalayas in Nepal, far southwestern Tibet, northern India, northern Pakistan, Bhutan and possibly Afghanistan..

children.name: Semnopithecus priam
children.description: The tufted gray langur (Semnopithecus priam), also known as Madras gray langur, and Coromandel sacred langur, is an Old World monkey, one of the species of langurs..

children.name: Semnopithecus dussumieri
children.description: Southern plains gray langur was the common name ascribed to Semnopithecus dussumieri by Mammal Species of the World (3rd edition) in 2005..

children.name: Semnopithecus hector
children.description: The Tarai gray langur (Semnopithecus hector) is an Old World monkey, and was formerly considered a subspecies of the northern plains gray langur..

children.name: Semnopithecus hypoleucos
children.description: The black-footed gray langur (Semnopithecus hypoleucos) is an Old World monkey, one of the species of langurs..

children.name: Semnopithecus ajax
children.description: The Kashmir gray langur (Semnopithecus ajax) is an Old World monkey, one of the langur species..

children.name: Trachypithecus
children.description: Lutungs, or banded leaf monkeys — a diverse group of colobine monkeys distributed across South and Southeast Asia. Many species are born bright orange and gradually darken to their adult colouration, creating striking nursery groups within troops.

children.name: Trachypithecus cristatus
children.description: The silvery lutung (Trachypithecus cristatus), also known as the silvered leaf monkey or the silvery langur, is an Old World monkey.

children.name: Trachypithecus phayrei
children.description: Phayre's leaf monkey (Trachypithecus phayrei), also known as Phayre's langur, is a species of Old World monkey native to South Asia and Southeast Asia, namely India, Bangladesh, and Myanmar..

children.name: Trachypithecus obscurus
children.description: The dusky leaf monkey (Trachypithecus obscurus), also known as the spectacled langur or the spectacled leaf monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Trachypithecus auratus
children.description: The East Javan langur (Trachypithecus auratus), also known as the ebony lutung, Javan langur or Javan lutung, is an Old World monkey from the Colobinae subfamily..

children.name: Trachypithecus francoisi
children.description: François' langur (Trachypithecus francoisi), also known as Francois' leaf monkey, the Tonkin leaf monkey, or the white side-burned black langur is a species of Old World monkey and the type species of its species group..

children.name: Trachypithecus delacouri
children.description: Delacour's langur or Delacour's lutung (Trachypithecus delacouri) is a critically endangered species of Old World monkey endemic to northern Vietnam..

children.name: Trachypithecus poliocephalus
children.description: The Cat Ba langur (Trachypithecus poliocephalus), also known as the golden-headed langur, is a critically endangered species of langur endemic to Cát Bà Island, Vietnam..

children.name: Trachypithecus germaini
children.description: Germain's langur (Trachypithecus germaini) is an Old World monkey native to Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam..

children.name: Trachypithecus pileatus
children.description: The capped langur (Trachypithecus pileatus) is a primate species in the family Cercopithecidae native to subtropical and tropical dry forests in northeast India, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar.

children.name: Trachypithecus johnii
children.description: The Nilgiri langur (Semnopithecus johnii) is an Asian langur of the Old World monkey.

children.name: Trachypithecus vetulus
children.description: The purple-faced langur (Semnopithecus vetulus), also known as the purple-faced leaf monkey, is a species of Old World monkey that is endemic to Sri Lanka..

children.name: Trachypithecus hatinhensis
children.description: The Hatinh langur (Trachypithecus hatinhensis) is a highly threatened Old World monkey found in limestone forests in Vietnam, primarily in the Quảng Bình Province.

children.name: Trachypithecus laotum
children.description: The Laotian langur or white-browed black langur (Trachypithecus laotum) is a species of the primate family Cercopithecidae that is endemic to Laos in Southeast Asia.

children.name: Trachypithecus geei
children.description: Gee's golden langur (Trachypithecus geei), also known as simply the golden langur, is an Old World monkey found in a small region of Western Assam, India and the neighboring foothills of the Black Mountains of Bhutan..

children.name: Trachypithecus shortridgei
children.description: The Shortridge's langur (Trachypithecus shortridgei) is an Old World monkey native to Burma and China..

children.name: Trachypithecus barbei
children.description: The Tenasserim lutung (Trachypithecus barbei) is a species of Old World monkey.

children.name: Trachypithecus crepusculus
children.description: The Indochinese grey langur (Trachypithecus crepusculus) is a species of Old World monkey native to East and Southeast Asia..

children.name: Presbytis
children.description: Surilis or Sunda leaf monkeys are a diverse group of colobines endemic to the Sunda region — Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra, Borneo, and adjacent islands. Most species are characterised by brightly coloured neonates, and several are distinguished only by subtle differences in pelage or crest shape.

children.name: Presbytis comata
children.description: The Javan surili (Presbytis comata) is a vulnerable species of Old World monkey endemic to the western half of Java, Indonesia, a biodiversity hotspot.

children.name: Presbytis femoralis
children.description: The Raffles' banded langur (Presbytis femoralis), also known as the banded leaf monkey or banded surili, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Presbytis frontata
children.description: The white-fronted surili (Presbytis frontata) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae, the Old World monkeys..

children.name: Presbytis hosei
children.description: Hose's langur (Presbytis hosei) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae endemic to the island of Borneo, including Brunei, Kalimantan (Indonesia), and East Malaysia..

children.name: Presbytis melalophos
children.description: The black-crested Sumatran langur is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae. It is endemic to Sumatra in Indonesia. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical dry forests.

children.name: Presbytis rubicunda
children.description: The maroon langur, maroon leaf monkey, or red leaf monkey (Presbytis rubicunda) is a member of the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Presbytis siamensis
children.description: The white-thighed surili (Presbytis siamensis) is a species of primate from the family of old world monkeys (Cercopithecidae)..

children.name: Presbytis thomasi
children.description: Thomas's langur (Presbytis thomasi), also known as the North Sumatran leaf monkey or Thomas's leaf monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Presbytis chrysomelas
children.description: The Sarawak surili, and it has been considered a subspecies of P.

children.name: Presbytis natunae
children.description: The Natuna Island surili (Presbytis natunae) is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Presbytis canicrus
children.description: Miller's langur (Presbytis canicrus), also known as Miller's grizzled langur or Kutai grey langur, is a species of leaf monkey..

children.name: Pygathrix
children.description: The douc langurs are among the most brilliantly coloured primates in the world, with multicoloured facial skin and vivid patterned coats. Confined to the forests of Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia, all three species are severely threatened by the illegal wildlife trade and habitat loss.

children.name: Pygathrix nemaeus
children.description: The red-shanked douc (Pygathrix nemaeus) is an arboreal and diurnal Old World monkey belonging to the Colobinae subfamily..

children.name: Pygathrix nigripes
children.description: The black-shanked douc (Pygathrix nigripes) is an endangered species of douc found mostly in the forests of Eastern Cambodia, with some smaller populations in Southern Vietnam..

children.name: Pygathrix cinerea
children.description: The grey-shanked douc langur (Pygathrix cinerea) is a douc species native to the Vietnamese provinces of Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi, Bình Định, Kon Tum, and Gia Lai..

children.name: Rhinopithecus
children.description: Snub-nosed monkeys are specialised high-altitude colobines of China and adjacent Southeast Asia, bearing upturned nostrils without an external nasal bone. They are remarkable for inhabiting some of the coldest environments occupied by any primate, foraging in snow-covered forests.

children.name: Rhinopithecus roxellana
children.description: The golden snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus roxellana) is an Old World monkey in the subfamily Colobinae..

children.name: Rhinopithecus bieti
children.description: The black-and-white snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus bieti), also known as the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey, is a large black and white primate that lives only in the southern Chinese province of Yunnan, where it is known to the locals as the Yunnan golden hair monkey (Chinese: 滇金丝猴) and the black-and-white snub-nosed monkey (黑白仰鼻猴)..

children.name: Rhinopithecus brelichi
children.description: The gray snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus brelichi), also known as Brelich's snub-nosed monkey, Guizhou snub-nosed monkey, and Guizhou golden monkey, is a species of primate in the family Cercopithecidae..

children.name: Rhinopithecus avunculus
children.description: The Tonkin snub-nosed monkey or Dollman's snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus avunculus) is a slender-bodied arboreal Old World monkey endemic to northern Vietnam..

children.name: Rhinopithecus strykeri
children.description: The Myanmar snub-nosed monkey or Burmese snub-nosed monkey or black snub-nosed monkey (Rhinopithecus strykeri) is a critically endangered species of colobine monkey described in 2010 in northern Myanmar..

children.name: Simias
children.description: A monotypic genus for the pig-tailed langur or simakobu, an unusual colobine endemic to the Mentawai Islands of Indonesia. Unlike most colobines, it has a short, pig-like tail and inhabits both primary and secondary forest.

children.name: Simias concolor
children.description: The pig-tailed langur (Simias concolor), monotypic in genus Simias, is a large Old World monkey, endemic to several small islands off the coast of Sumatra in Indonesia..

children.name: Nasalis
children.description: The proboscis monkey is one of the most distinctive primates, the male bearing an enormous pendulous nose that amplifies vocalizations to attract mates. A highly specialised semi-aquatic species endemic to the mangroves and riverine forests of Borneo.

children.name: Nasalis larvatus
children.description: The proboscis monkey or long-nosed monkey (Nasalis larvatus) is an arboreal Old World monkey with an unusually large nose (or proboscis), a reddish-brown skin color and a long tail.

families.name: Platyrrhini
families.taxonomicNote: Platyrrhini parvorder — treated here as a family-level group spanning Cebidae, Callitrichidae, Atelidae, and Pitheciidae.

children.name: Cebus
children.description: Gracile capuchins are small to medium-sized monkeys with a reputation as the most intelligent New World primates, capable of tool use — cracking nuts with stones — and complex social manipulation. Widespread across Central and South American forests.

children.name: Cebus capucinus
children.description: The Colombian white-faced capuchin (Cebus capucinus), also known as the Colombian white-headed capuchin or Colombian white-throated capuchin, is a medium-sized New World monkey of the family Cebidae, subfamily Cebinae..

children.name: Cebus olivaceus
children.description: The wedge-capped capuchin or Guianan weeper capuchin (Cebus olivaceus) is a capuchin monkey from South America..

children.name: Cebus albifrons
children.description: Humboldt's white-fronted capuchin (Cebus albifrons) is a species of gracile capuchin monkey..

children.name: Cebus kaapori
children.description: The Kaapori capuchin (Cebus kaapori), also known as the Ka'apor capuchin, is a species of frugivorous, gracile capuchin endemic to the Brazilian Amazon.

children.name: Cebus imitator
children.description: The Panamanian white-faced capuchin (Cebus imitator), also known as the Panamanian white-headed capuchin or Central American white-faced capuchin, is a medium-sized New World monkey of the family Cebidae, subfamily Cebinae.

children.name: Sapajus
children.description: Robust capuchins of South America, recently split from Cebus, are stout-bodied monkeys known for their exceptional tool use including the systematic cracking of hard palm nuts with heavy stones — behaviour passed culturally between generations.

children.name: Sapajus apella
children.description: The tufted capuchin (Sapajus apella), also known as brown capuchin, black-capped capuchin, or pin monkey, is a New World primate from South America and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita..

children.name: Sapajus libidinosus
children.description: The black-striped capuchin (Sapajus libidinosus), also known as the bearded capuchin, is a New World monkey in the family Cebidae..

children.name: Sapajus nigritus
children.description: The black capuchin (Sapajus nigritus), also known as the black-horned capuchin, is a capuchin monkey from the Atlantic Forest in south-eastern Brazil and far north-eastern Argentina.

children.name: Sapajus robustus
children.description: The crested capuchin or robust tufted capuchin (Sapajus robustus) is a species of robust capuchin monkey.

children.name: Sapajus xanthosternos
children.description: The golden-bellied capuchin (Sapajus xanthosternos), also known as the yellow-breasted or buff-headed capuchin, is a species of New World or neotropical monkey..

children.name: Sapajus flavius
children.description: The blond capuchin (Sapajus flavius) is a species of capuchin monkey endemic to northeastern Brazil.

children.name: Sapajus cay
children.description: Azaras's capuchin or hooded capuchin (Sapajus cay) is a species of robust capuchin..

children.name: Sapajus macrocephalus
children.description: The large-headed capuchin (Sapajus apella macrocephalus) is a subspecies of the tufted capuchin monkey from South America..

children.name: Saimiri
children.description: Squirrel monkeys are small, hyperactive primates of Amazonian and Central American forests, living in large, noisy troops of up to 500 individuals. Despite their small size, they have the largest brain-to-body ratio of any primate.

children.name: Saimiri sciureus
children.description: The Guianan squirrel monkey (Saimiri sciureus) is a species of squirrel monkey from Guiana, Venezuela and Brazil..

children.name: Saimiri boliviensis
children.description: The black-capped squirrel monkey (Saimiri boliviensis) is a species of New-World monkey native to the upper Amazon basin in Bolivia, western Brazil and eastern Peru..

children.name: Saimiri oerstedii
children.description: The Central American squirrel monkey (Saimiri oerstedii), also known as the red-backed squirrel monkey, is a squirrel monkey species from the Pacific coast of Costa Rica and Panama..

children.name: Saimiri ustus
children.description: The bare-eared squirrel monkey (Saimiri ustus) is a squirrel monkey endemic to Brazil and possibly eastern Bolivia..

children.name: Saimiri vanzolinii
children.description: The black squirrel monkey (Saimiri vanzolinii), also known as the blackish squirrel monkey or black-headed squirrel monkey, is a small New World primate, endemic to the central Amazon in Brazil..

children.name: Saimiri cassiquiarensis
children.description: Humboldt's squirrel monkey is a species of squirrel monkey from Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela. It had previously been considered a subspecies of the common squirrel monkey, S. sciureus, but was elevated to full species status based on a genetic study by Carretero-Pinzón in 2009.

children.name: Alouatta
children.description: Howler monkeys are the loudest land animals on Earth — their roars, produced by an enlarged hyoid bone, carry up to 5 km through dense forest and serve as long-distance territorial announcements. They are the most widely distributed New World monkeys.

children.name: Alouatta seniculus
children.description: The Colombian red howler or Venezuelan red howler (Alouatta seniculus) is a South American species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, found in the western Amazon Basin in Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Brazil..

children.name: Alouatta palliata
children.description: The mantled howler (Alouatta palliata) is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, from Central and South America.

children.name: Alouatta caraya
children.description: The black howler or black-and-gold howler, is among the largest New World monkeys and a member of the Alouatta genus. The black howler is distributed in areas of South America such as Paraguay, southern Brazil, eastern Bolivia, northern Argentina, and Uruguay. This species is sexually dimorphic, with adult males having entirely black fur and adult females and babies of both sexes having an overall golden colouring; which emphasizes black-and-gold in the name.

children.name: Alouatta pigra
children.description: The Yucatán black howler, or Guatemalan black howler, (Alouatta pigra) is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, from Central America..

children.name: Alouatta guariba
children.description: The brown howler (Alouatta guariba), also known as brown howler monkey, is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey that lives in forests in south-eastern Brazil and far north-eastern Argentina (Misiones).

children.name: Alouatta belzebul
children.description: The red-handed howler (Alouatta belzebul) is a vulnerable species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey..

children.name: Alouatta nigerrima
children.description: The Amazon black howler (Alouatta nigerrima) is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to the south-central Amazon in Brazil..

children.name: Alouatta discolor
children.description: Spix's red-handed howler (Alouatta discolor) is a species of Howler monkey native to the southeastern Amazon in Brazil..

children.name: Alouatta sara
children.description: The Bolivian red howler is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Bolivia. It can be found in rain forests, including riverine and seasonally flooded forests.

children.name: Alouatta puruensis
children.description: The Purús red howler (Alouatta puruensis) is a species of howler monkey native to Brazil, Peru and north of Bolivia..

children.name: Alouatta macconnelli
children.description: The Guyanan red howler (Alouatta macconnelli) is a species of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, native to Suriname, Guyana, Trinidad, French Guiana, Venezuela and Brazil..

children.name: Alouatta coibensis
children.description: The Coiba Island howler (Alouatta coibensis) is a type of howler monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Panama..

children.name: Ateles
children.description: Spider monkeys are among the most acrobatic of all primates, using their prehensile tail as a fifth limb to swing through the forest canopy. They have the longest arms relative to body size of any New World monkey and are important seed dispersers in Neotropical forests.

children.name: Ateles geoffroyi
children.description: Geoffroy's spider monkey (Ateles geoffroyi), also known as the black-handed spider monkey or the Central American spider monkey, is a species of spider monkey, a type of New World monkey, from Central America, parts of Mexico and possibly a small portion of Colombia..

children.name: Ateles paniscus
children.description: The red-faced spider monkey (Ateles paniscus), also known as the Guiana spider monkey or red-faced black spider monkey, is a species of spider monkey found in the rain forests in northern South America..

children.name: Ateles belzebuth
children.description: The white-bellied spider monkey (Ateles belzebuth), also known as the white-fronted or long-haired spider monkey, is an endangered species of spider monkey, a type of New World monkey..

children.name: Ateles chamek
children.description: The Peruvian spider monkey (Ateles chamek), also known as the black-faced black spider monkey, is a species of spider monkey that lives in Peru, as well as in Brazil and in Bolivia..

children.name: Ateles hybridus
children.description: The brown spider monkey or variegated spider monkey (Ateles hybridus) is a critically endangered species of spider monkey, a type of New World monkey, from forests in northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela..

children.name: Ateles marginatus
children.description: The white-cheeked spider monkey (Ateles marginatus) is a species of spider monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Ateles fusciceps
children.description: The black-headed spider monkey (Ateles fusciceps) is a species of spider monkey from Central and South America, specifically Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama..

children.name: Lagothrix
children.description: Woolly monkeys are large, heavy-bodied primates of Amazonian and Andean foothill forests, named for their dense, soft fur. They are among the most frugivorous of all primates and critical seed dispersers of large-seeded trees in western Amazonia.

children.name: Lagothrix lagothricha
children.description: The common woolly monkey, brown woolly monkey, or Humboldt's woolly monkey (Lagothrix lagothricha) is a woolly monkey from Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Brazil, and Venezuela..

children.name: Lagothrix cana
children.description: The gray woolly monkey (Lagothrix lagothricha cana) or Geoffroy's woolly monkey is a subspecies of the common woolly monkey from South America..

children.name: Lagothrix poeppigii
children.description: The silvery woolly monkey (Lagothrix lagothricha poeppigii), also known as Poeppig's woolly monkey or the red woolly monkey, is a subspecies of the common woolly monkey from South America..

children.name: Lagothrix lugens
children.description: The Colombian woolly monkey (Lagothrix lagothricha lugens) is a critically endangered subspecies of the common woolly monkey from Colombia..

children.name: Lagothrix tschudii
children.description: The Peruvian woolly monkey, named for Swiss naturalist Johann Jakob von Tschudi, is restricted to the Peruvian and Bolivian Amazon. It inhabits lowland tropical forest and is Endangered due to hunting and habitat loss. Recent molecular analysis confirmed it as a species distinct from the widespread Lagothrix lagothricha.

children.name: Brachyteles
children.description: Muriquis, or woolly spider monkeys, are the largest New World primates and are endemic to the Atlantic Forest of Brazil. They are almost exclusively leaf-eating and are remarkable for their 'peaceful' egalitarian social system in which males rarely fight and females have high social autonomy.

children.name: Brachyteles arachnoides
children.description: The southern muriqui (Brachyteles arachnoides) is a muriqui (woolly spider monkey) species endemic to Brazil.

children.name: Brachyteles hypoxanthus
children.description: The northern muriqui (Brachyteles hypoxanthus) is one of two species of muriqui.

children.name: Oreonax
children.description: A monotypic genus erected for the yellow-tailed woolly monkey of the Peruvian Andes, separated from Lagothrix on molecular grounds. It is among the rarest and most endangered of all primates.

children.name: Oreonax flavicauda
children.description: The yellow-tailed woolly monkey (Lagothrix flavicauda) is a species of New World monkey endemic to Peru..

children.name: Callithrix
children.description: Atlantic Forest marmosets are tiny, squirrel-sized primates with distinctive ear tufts and claws adapted for clinging to tree bark to gouge holes and feed on gum. They reliably give birth to non-identical twins and practise extensive cooperative infant care.

children.name: Callithrix jacchus
children.description: The common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus), also called white-tufted marmoset or white-tufted-ear marmoset, is a New World monkey.

children.name: Callithrix penicillata
children.description: The black-tufted marmoset (Callithrix penicillata) is a species of New World monkey that lives primarily in the Neotropical gallery forests of the Brazilian Central Plateau..

children.name: Callithrix geoffroyi
children.description: The white-headed marmoset (Callithrix geoffroyi), also known as the tufted-ear marmoset, Geoffroy's marmoset, or Geoffrey's marmoset, is a marmoset endemic to forests in eastern Brazil, where it is native to Bahia, Espírito Santo, and Minas Gerais, and introduced to Santa Catarina..

children.name: Callithrix aurita
children.description: The buffy-tufted marmoset (Callithrix aurita), also known as the buffy tufted-ear marmoset or white-eared marmoset, is a New World monkey that lives in the forests on the Atlantic coast of southeast Brazil..

children.name: Callithrix flaviceps
children.description: The buffy-headed marmoset (Callithrix flaviceps) is a rare species of marmoset endemic to the rainforests of south-eastern Brazil..

children.name: Callithrix kuhlii
children.description: Wied's marmoset (Callithrix kuhlii), also known as Wied's black-tufted-ear marmoset, is a New World monkey that lives in tropical and subtropical forests of eastern Brazil..

children.name: Cebuella
children.description: Pygmy marmosets are the world's smallest monkeys and among the smallest primates, weighing as little as 100 g. They are highly specialised gummivores, excavating tree bark with their distinctive procumbent lower incisors to create sap-wells that form the core of their small home ranges.

children.name: Cebuella pygmaea
children.description: The western pygmy marmoset (Cebuella pygmaea) is a marmoset species, a very small New World monkey found in the northwestern Amazon rainforest in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru..

children.name: Cebuella niveiventris
children.description: The eastern pygmy marmoset (Cebuella niveiventris) is a marmoset species, a very small New World monkey, found in the southwestern Amazon rainforest in Bolivia, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru..

children.name: Mico
children.description: Amazonian marmosets, recently split from Callithrix, are a diverse group of small primates endemic to the Brazilian Amazon, many of which have only been described in recent decades as their remote habitats have become accessible.

children.name: Mico argentatus
children.description: The silvery marmoset (Mico argentatus) is a New World monkey that lives in the eastern Amazon Rainforest in Brazil.

children.name: Mico melanurus
children.description: The black-tailed marmoset (Mico melanurus) is a species of New World monkey from central South America, where it ranges from the south-central Amazon in Brazil, south through the Pantanal and eastern Bolivia, to the Chaco in far northern Paraguay..

children.name: Mico humeralifer
children.description: The Santarem marmoset (Mico humeralifer), also known as the black and white tassel-ear marmoset, is a marmoset endemic to the Brazilian states of Amazonas and Pará.

children.name: Mico chrysoleucos
children.description: The gold-and-white marmoset is named for its striking golden-yellow and white pelage and is endemic to a small area of the Brazilian Amazon between the lower Juruena and Tapajós rivers. It was described by Spix in 1823 from a small collection area. As with many Mico marmosets, the boundaries of its range are delimited by major river barriers — a pattern driving the extraordinary diversity of this genus.

children.name: Mico nigriceps
children.description: The black-headed marmoset (Mico nigriceps) is a marmoset species endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Mico emiliae
children.description: The Emilia's marmoset (Mico emiliae), also known as Snethlage's marmoset, is a marmoset endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Mico manicorensis
children.description: The Marca's marmoset (Mico marcai) is a species of marmoset that is endemic to the Amazon, in the Aripuanã-Manicoré interfluvium in Brazil..

children.name: Mico marcai
children.description: The Marca's marmoset (Mico marcai) is a species of marmoset that is endemic to the Amazon, in the Aripuanã-Manicoré interfluvium in Brazil..

children.name: Mico intermedius
children.description: The Hershkovitz's marmoset (Mico intermedius), also known as the Aripuanã marmoset is a marmoset species endemic to the south-central Amazon rainforest in Brazil..

children.name: Mico leucippe
children.description: The white marmoset (Mico leucippe), or golden-white bare-ear marmoset, is a species of marmoset, a small monkey endemic to the Amazon rainforest in Pará, Brazil.

children.name: Mico acariensis
children.description: The Rio Acarí marmoset (Mico acariensis) is a marmoset species endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Mico saterei
children.description: The Satéré marmoset (Mico saterei) is a marmoset species endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Mico oryzivora
children.description: The rice marmoset — named from an early, erroneous belief that it raided rice crops — is endemic to the Marajó Island and adjacent lower Amazon delta. It is unique among Mico in occupying an island and deltaic environment rather than upland Amazonian forest. It is considered Vulnerable due to the increasingly rapid clearance of vegetation on Marajó Island for cattle farming.

children.name: Mico roscidus
children.description: The wet marmoset is a distinctive species with dark grey-agouti dorsum and whitish underparts, known only from a restricted area of Rondônia and Mato Grosso in Brazil. Its common name reflects the grey-toned fur that Elliot Thomas coined as 'roscidus' (dewy). Deforestation in Rondônia has been severe and rapid, threatening this species across much of its limited range.

children.name: Mico rondoni
children.description: Rondon's marmoset (Mico rondoni), also known as the Rondônia marmoset, is a small species of monkey from the family Callitrichidae found in the south-western Amazon in Brazil..

children.name: Callimico
children.description: Goeldi's monkey is an anomalous callitrichid that combines marmoset-like morphology with tamarin-like features: it gives birth to single offspring (unlike the typical twin-births of marmosets) and retains third molars absent in other callitrichids. It is the sole member of its genus.

children.name: Callimico goeldii
children.description: Goeldi's marmoset, or Goeldi's monkey (Callimico goeldii), is a small New World monkey found on the South American continent, mainly in the upper Amazon basin of Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, and Perú.

children.name: Saguinus
children.description: The true tamarins — a diverse genus of small, long-clawed primates of Central and South American forests, often bearing elaborate facial ornamentation including mustaches, crests, and manes. Like marmosets, they routinely produce twins and live in cooperatively breeding family groups.

children.name: Saguinus oedipus
children.description: The cotton-top tamarin (Saguinus oedipus) is a small New World monkey weighing less than 0.5 kg (1.1 lb)..

children.name: Saguinus imperator
children.description: The emperor tamarin (Saguinus imperator) is a species of tamarin monkey allegedly named for its beard's resemblance to that of the German emperor Wilhelm II.

children.name: Saguinus midas
children.description: The golden-handed tamarin (Saguinus midas), also known as the red-handed tamarin or Midas tamarin, is a New World monkey belonging to the family Callitrichidae..

children.name: Saguinus fuscicollis
children.description: The brown-mantled tamarin (Leontocebus fuscicollis), also known as Spix's saddle-back tamarin, is a species of saddle-back tamarin..

children.name: Saguinus mystax
children.description: The moustached tamarin (Saguinus mystax) is a New World monkey and a species of tamarin.

children.name: Saguinus labiatus
children.description: The white-lipped tamarin (Saguinus labiatus), also known as the red-bellied tamarin, is a tamarin which lives in the Amazon area of Brazil and  Bolivia..

children.name: Saguinus nigricollis
children.description: The black-mantled tamarin, Leontocebus nigricollis, is a species of saddle-back tamarin from the northwestern Amazon in far western Brazil, southeastern Colombia, north-eastern Peru and eastern Ecuador..

children.name: Saguinus bicolor
children.description: thumb|Pied tamarin in captivity The pied tamarin (Saguinus bicolor), sometimes referred to as the Brazilian bare-faced tamarin, is a critically endangered species of primate found in a restricted area of the Brazilian Amazon rainforest.

children.name: Saguinus leucopus
children.description: The white-footed tamarin (Saguinus leucopus) is a tamarin species endemic to Colombia..

children.name: Saguinus geoffroyi
children.description: Geoffroy's tamarin (Saguinus geoffroyi), also known as the Panamanian, red-crested or rufous-naped tamarin, is a tamarin, a type of small monkey, found in Panama and Colombia..

children.name: Saguinus inustus
children.description: The mottle-faced tamarin (Saguinus inustus) is a species of tamarin from South America..

children.name: Saguinus martinsi
children.description: Martins's tamarin (Saguinus martinsi) or Martin's ochraceous bare-face tamarin, is a species of tamarin endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Saguinus graellsi
children.description: Graells's tamarin, Leontocebus nigricollis graellsi, is a subspecies of the black-mantled tamarin from the northwestern Amazon in southeastern Colombia, eastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru..

children.name: Saguinus pileatus
children.description: The red-capped tamarin (Saguinus mystax pileatus), is subspecies of moustached tamarin from South America..

children.name: Saguinus tripartitus
children.description: The golden-mantled tamarin (Leontocebus tripartitus) is a tamarin species from South America..

children.name: Saguinus illigeri
children.description: Illiger's saddle-back tamarin (Leontocebus illigeri) is a species of saddle-back tamarin, a type of small monkey from South America..

children.name: Saguinus weddelli
children.description: Weddell's saddle-back tamarin (Leontocebus weddelli) is a species of saddle-back tamarin, a type of small monkey from South America..

children.name: Saguinus melanoleucus
children.description: The white-mantled tamarin, Leontocebus weddelli melanoleucus,  is a subspecies of Weddell's saddle-back tamarin, a tamarin monkey from South America..

children.name: Saguinus ursulus
children.description: The eastern black-handed tamarin (Saguinus ursulus) is a species of tamarin endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Saguinus niger
children.description: The black tamarin (Saguinus niger) or western black-handed tamarin is a species of tamarin endemic to Brazil.

children.name: Leontopithecus
children.description: Lion tamarins are among the most endangered primates in the world — brilliantly coloured small monkeys with a mane of long hair framing the face, restricted to the Atlantic Forest fragments of southeastern Brazil. Intensive conservation breeding programmes have significantly improved their numbers.

children.name: Leontopithecus rosalia
children.description: The golden lion tamarin (Leontopithecus rosalia; ), less commonly known as the golden lion marmoset, is a small New World monkey of the family Callitrichidae.

children.name: Leontopithecus chrysomelas
children.description: The golden-headed lion tamarin (Leontopithecus chrysomelas), also the golden-headed tamarin, is a lion tamarin endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Leontopithecus chrysopygus
children.description: The black lion tamarin (Leontopithecus chrysopygus), also known as the golden-rumped lion tamarin, is a lion tamarin endemic to the Brazilian state of São Paulo, almost exclusively at the Morro do Diabo State Park..

children.name: Leontopithecus caissara
children.description: The black-faced lion tamarin or Superagüi lion tamarin (Leontopithecus caissara) is a small New World monkey of the family Callitrichidae..

children.name: Aotus
children.description: Night monkeys, or owl monkeys, are the only truly nocturnal anthropoid primates — a unique adaptation among higher primates. They have enormous, forward-facing eyes adapted for low-light vision and live in small, strictly monogamous family groups in which the father carries infants.

children.name: Aotus trivirgatus
children.description: The three-striped night monkey (Aotus trivirgatus), also known as northern night monkey or northern owl monkey, is one of several species of owl monkeys currently recognised..

children.name: Aotus azarae
children.description: Azara's night monkey (Aotus azarae), also known as the Azara's owl monkey, the southern night monkey, or the mirikiná, is a night monkey species from South America..

children.name: Aotus vociferans
children.description: Spix's night monkey (Aotus vociferans), also known as the Colombian gray night monkey, noisy night monkey and Spix's owl monkey, is a night monkey species from South America..

children.name: Aotus nancymaae
children.description: Nancy Ma's night monkey (Aotus nancymaae) is a night monkey species from South America..

children.name: Aotus nigriceps
children.description: The black-headed night monkey (Aotus nigriceps) is a night monkey species from South America..

children.name: Aotus lemurinus
children.description: The gray-bellied night monkey (Aotus lemurinus), also called the grey-legged douroucouli or lemurine owl monkey, is a small New World monkey of the family Aotidae..

children.name: Aotus miconax
children.description: The Peruvian night monkey (Aotus miconax), also known as the Andean night monkey, is a nocturnal New World monkey endemic to northern Peru..

children.name: Aotus brumbacki
children.description: Brumback's night monkey (Aotus brumbacki) is a species of night monkey found in Colombia..

children.name: Aotus griseimembra
children.description: The gray-handed night monkey (Aotus griseimembra) is a species of night monkey formerly considered a subspecies of Gray-bellied night monkey of the family Aotidae..

children.name: Aotus zonalis
children.description: The Panamanian night monkey or Chocoan night monkey (Aotus zonalis) is a species of night monkey formerly considered a subspecies of the gray-bellied night monkey of the family Aotidae..

children.name: Callicebus
children.description: Titi monkeys of the Callicebus group are small, shy primates of Amazonian forests, famous for their spectacular dawn duets between mated pairs and their habit of tail-twining — sitting side by side with tails entwined as a social bonding behaviour.

children.name: Callicebus torquatus
children.description: The collared titi monkey (Cheracebus torquatus) is a species of titi, a type of New World monkey..

children.name: Callicebus lugens
children.description: The black titi monkey (Cheracebus lugens), is a species of titi, a type of New World monkey, from South America..

children.name: Plecturocebus
children.description: Plecturocebus is one of three genera into which titi monkeys were recently divided. These are small, monogamous, frugivorous primates of Amazonian forests characterised by soft thick fur and the habit of duetting at dawn with their lifelong mates.

children.name: Plecturocebus moloch
children.description: The red-bellied titi monkey or dusky titi (Plecturocebus moloch) is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Plecturocebus donacophilus
children.description: The white-eared titi monkey (Plecturocebus donacophilus) also known as the Bolivian titi or Bolivian gray titi, is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, from eastern Bolivia and an area of western Brazil..

children.name: Plecturocebus cupreus
children.description: The coppery titi monkey or red titi monkey is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, from South America. They are found in the Amazon of Brazil and Peru, and perhaps northern Bolivia. It was described as Callithrix cupreus in 1823.

children.name: Plecturocebus caligatus
children.description: The chestnut-bellied titi monkey (Plecturocebus caligatus), also called booted titi, is a species of titi monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to Brazil..

children.name: Plecturocebus aureipalatii
children.description: The Madidi titi monkey, also known as the GoldenPalace.com monkey or the golden palace monkey, is a titi, a kind of New World monkey, discovered in western Bolivia's Madidi National Park in 2004..

children.name: Plecturocebus caquetensis
children.description: The Caquetá titi monkey (Plecturocebus caquetensis), also known as the red-bearded titi or the bushy-bearded titi, is a species of titi monkey endemic to Colombia found in the Department of Caquetá region..

children.name: Plecturocebus lucifer
children.description: The Lucifer titi inhabits forests of the western Amazon in Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia and is part of the torquatus group, with rich reddish-brown underparts. It is listed as Least Concern and occurs in several protected areas including the Yasuni and Cuyabeno reserves in Ecuador. Its population status is not well quantified but it appears stable in undisturbed forest.

children.name: Pithecia
children.description: Sakis are medium-sized pitheciid primates of Amazonian forests, characterised by dense, rough coats and bushy tails used for balance. They are highly specialised seed predators, using their procumbent incisors and strong jaw muscles to crack hard-coated seeds that other primates cannot open.

children.name: Pithecia pithecia
children.description: The white-faced saki (Pithecia pithecia), is a species of New World saki monkey..

children.name: Pithecia monachus
children.description: The monk saki (Pithecia monachus) also known as Geoffroy's monk saki, is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey, from South America.

children.name: Pithecia irrorata
children.description: The Rio Tapajós saki or Gray's bald-faced saki (Pithecia irrorata) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey, from South America..

children.name: Pithecia albicans
children.description: The white-footed saki, buffy saki or white saki (Pithecia albicans) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey, endemic to western Brazil south of the Amazon..

children.name: Pithecia aequatorialis
children.description: The equatorial saki (Pithecia aequatorialis), also called the red-bearded saki, is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey.

children.name: Pithecia hirsuta
children.description: The hairy saki (Pithecia hirsuta) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey.

children.name: Pithecia chrysocephala
children.description: The golden-faced saki (Pithecia chrysocephala) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey..

children.name: Pithecia vanzolinii
children.description: Vanzolini's bald-faced saki (Pithecia vanzolinii) is a species of saki monkey, a type of New World monkey..

children.name: Chiropotes
children.description: Bearded sakis are specialised seed predators of Amazonian and Guiana Shield forests, distinguished by bilobed parietal swellings on the head and prominent beards. They are highly mobile and travel large distances daily in large groups to exploit widely dispersed hard-seeded fruit resources.

children.name: Chiropotes satanas
children.description: The black bearded saki (Chiropotes satanas) is a species of New World monkey, native to the Amazon rainforest of South America, specifically to an area of north-eastern Brazil..

children.name: Chiropotes albinasus
children.description: The white-nosed saki (Chiropotes albinasus) is a species of bearded saki, a type of New World monkey, endemic to the south-central Amazon rainforest in Brazil..

children.name: Chiropotes chiropotes
children.description: The red-backed bearded saki (Chiropotes chiropotes) is a New-World monkey, from South America..

children.name: Chiropotes israelita
children.description: The brown-backed bearded saki (Chiropotes israelita) is one of five species of bearded saki, a type of New World monkey..

children.name: Chiropotes utahickae
children.description: Uta Hick's bearded saki (Chiropotes utahicki) is an endangered species of bearded saki, a type of New World monkey..

children.name: Cacajao
children.description: Uakaris are highly distinctive pitheciid primates with bald, vividly coloured red faces and unusually short tails for New World monkeys. They are specialised for flooded and seasonally inundated forests of the western Amazon and are among the most range-restricted of all primates.

children.name: Cacajao calvus
children.description: The bald uakari (Cacajao calvus) or bald-headed uakari is a small New World monkey characterized by a very short tail, a bright, crimson face, bald head, and long coat.

children.name: Cacajao melanocephalus
children.description: The golden-backed uakari (Cacajao melanocephalus) or black-headed uakari, is a New World primate from the family Pitheciidae..

children.name: Cacajao ayresi
children.description: The Aracá uakari (Cacajao ayresi), also known as the Ayres black uakari, is a newly described species of monkey from the northwest Brazilian Amazon..

children.name: Cacajao hosomi
children.description: The Neblina uakari (Cacajao hosomi) or black-headed uakari, is a newly described species of monkey from the far northwest Brazilian Amazon and adjacent southern Venezuela.

children.name: Lemur
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the ring-tailed lemur, arguably the most recognisable of all lemurs. Ring-tailed lemurs are unusual among strepsirrhines in being highly terrestrial and living in female-dominated groups. Their boldly banded tails are held aloft during social encounters.

children.name: Lemur catta
